text.p: Traders and analysts expect coffee to go higher on Monday.
Traders called it to open $20 up, while analysts are looking for a continuation of its rally.
Coffee is overbought to an extent not seen since January, independent analyst Elli Gifford said.
But on a daily basis, that did not concern her. Coffee was still set to go higher, she said.
Coffee-producing nations may suspend export quotas to try to cool an explosive rally that has lifted benchmark U.S. coffee bean futures to a 20-year high when they meet in London this week.

As roasters in the U.S. and Europe pass on their soaring costs to retailers, some of the 14 members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) worry that consumers will switch to tea or soft drinks.
Producers must show they they are not a cartel, said Paian Nainggolan of Indonesia.

On Friday, New York coffee futures pulled back in rollercoaster trading, pressured by speculative profit-taking and options-related selling on the heels of the market's recent sharp rally, traders said.
Also on Friday, LIFFE coffee futures shot up to 15-1/2 month high in a new rally fired by a wave of fund and technical buying. Trading was brisk.
Benchmark July clinched more than a six percent gain on the day as speculative and hedge funds swarmed into the market from the opening bell.
